script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Monday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed one point four one percent up on the session. A broad rally swept semiconductor names higher, with several key positions posting outsized gains heading into a critical earnings week.

Marvell Technology surged three point three one percent on Monday, leading all primary holdings. That move came as the Nasdaq Composite climbed two point one three percent, and chipmakers broadly caught a bid. The earnings calendar this week will determine whether that momentum holds.

The Nasdaq Composite gained two point one three percent on Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average touching a record high. Investor sentiment was lifted after President Trump signaled a restart of talks with Iran, easing oil prices and boosting risk appetite across equities. No major Federal Reserve commentary or economic data drove the session — this was a geopolitically catalyzed rally.

The top story on Monday belongs to Marvell Technology, which led all primary holdings with a gain of three point three one percent, riding a session that heavily rewarded semiconductor exposure. But the broader narrative shaping chipmaker sentiment centers on Advanced Micro Devices, which is set to report earnings this week and is drawing significant Wall Street attention. Citi issued a bullish note on Advanced Micro Devices on Monday, adding institutional momentum to the stock ahead of results. At the same time, Cathie Wood's Ark Invest disclosed it sold eleven point eight million dollars worth of Advanced Micro Devices shares on a single day in July — part of sixty-eight point one million dollars in total sales during the month. That divergence between a bullish Citi call and Ark's active trimming reflects the debate surrounding the stock ahead of earnings. Advanced Micro Devices gained one point seven eight percent on Monday.

Advanced Micro Devices was up one point seven eight percent on Monday's session. Beyond the Citi upgrade and the Ark sales disclosed for July, all eyes are now on earnings due this week. Analysts will be focused on data center revenue trajectory and any commentary on artificial intelligence chip demand. This remains the largest position in the portfolio at eight point three nine percent.

Micron Technology gained zero point seven nine percent on Monday's session. The session was not without turbulence — earlier reports indicated Apple is testing memory chips from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, a company that recently went public and surged to a market valuation near five hundred billion dollars. Micron recovered from early losses to close higher alongside the broader chip index, which rose just over one percent. The China competition angle bears watching as the quarter progresses.

Nvidia was up two point nine three percent on Monday's session. A Seeking Alpha analysis highlighted how Nvidia is using financial engineering — including guarantees and equity stakes in artificial intelligence labs — to accelerate its Vera Rubin architecture rollout while defending against custom chip competition. That structural strategy appears to be resonating with investors. Nvidia remains the third-largest position at seven point six one percent.

Broadcom gained zero point seven six percent on Monday's session. No company-specific news drove the move — the stock participated in the broad semiconductor rally. Broadcom's exposure to both networking infrastructure and custom artificial intelligence accelerators keeps it relevant to the prevailing demand narrative.

Intel was up zero point eight nine percent on Monday's session. The stock moved broadly in line with the sector without a specific catalyst. Intel's ongoing turnaround effort and competitive positioning in foundry services remain the key longer-term variables to monitor.

Applied Materials rose two point zero eight percent on Monday's session. No company-specific headlines drove the move, but equipment makers broadly benefited from renewed confidence in semiconductor capital expenditure cycles. Applied Materials' performance on Monday was the second-best among equipment names in the portfolio.

KLA Corporation was essentially flat, down zero point zero four percent on Monday's session. That slight underperformance relative to peers is not unusual for a session driven more by risk appetite than equipment-specific news. Upcoming earnings from chip manufacturers will inform the demand outlook for KLA's process control tools.

Marvell Technology surged three point three one percent on Monday's session, the strongest single-session gain among all primary holdings. No specific headline explained the move independently, suggesting the rally was technically driven and tied to the broader Nasdaq lift. Marvell's data center interconnect and custom silicon exposure continues to make it a favored name in the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.

Lam Research rose zero point five four percent on Monday's session. Like its equipment peers, Lam traded quietly without a distinct catalyst. The stock remains sensitive to memory and logic wafer start trends — Micron's competitive dynamics with Chinese rivals are worth monitoring for any downstream read-through.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing gained zero point four six percent on Monday's session. The stock lagged the broader rally, which is not uncommon given its dual sensitivity to geopolitical headlines and global fab utilization. No specific catalyst moved the name on Monday.

Three items to track in the next forty-eight hours. First, Advanced Micro Devices earnings — due this week — will be the single most important event for this portfolio, given the stock's eight point three nine percent weight. Second, Micron Technology's competitive positioning against ChangXin Memory Technologies warrants monitoring as new reports on Apple's chip testing surface. Third, watch for any continuation of the Iran ceasefire narrative, which drove Monday's Dow record and could sustain or reverse risk appetite across semiconductor names.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Advanced Micro Devices earnings will set the tone for the entire portfolio this week — position accordingly.
